ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On a long straight track, there is an F1 car. A safety car is moving at a constant speed of $10\mathrm{m/s}$ at a distance of $200\mathrm{m}$ ahead. At this moment, the F1 car starts from rest and accelerates at $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ to catch up.

1. When will the racing car catch up with the safety car
2. How far apart were they at the maximum distance before catching up with the safety car?
3. When the racing car just catches up with the safety car, the driver immediately brakes, causing the car to undergo uniformly decelerated linear motion with an acceleration of $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. How long will it take for the two cars to meet again? (Assume that the racing car can pass by the safety car without collision.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use an inertial coordinate along the track. Let the F1 car start at x_F(0)=0 and the safety car start at x_S(0)=200 m. The safety car moves at constant speed 10 m/s, so x_S=200+10t. The F1 car starts from rest with acceleration 2 m/s^2, so x_F=0+0\cdot t+\frac12(2)t^2=t^2. For the first catch-up, set x_F=x_S: t^2=200+10t, so t^2-10t-200=0. This factors as (t-20)(t+10)=0, giving the physical time t=20 s. The gap before catch-up is d(t)=x_S-x_F=200+10t-t^2. Its maximum occurs when d'(t)=10-2t=0, so t=5 s. Then d_max=200+10(5)-5^2=200+50-25=225 m. At the first catch-up time, the F1 speed is v=at=2(20)=40 m/s. After braking begins, use the stopping interpretation: the F1 decelerates from 40 m/s at 2 m/s^2, so it stops after 40/2=20 s. During those 20 s it travels v^2/(2a)=40^2/(2\cdot2)=400 m, while the safety car travels 10\cdot20=200 m, leaving the safety car 200 m behind the stopped F1. The safety car then takes another 200/10=20 s to reach it. Therefore the second meeting occurs 20+20=40 s after braking begins.

method.method_draft: Use relative-motion and velocity-time-area reasoning. Work in the safety car’s frame before catch-up. The initial relative position of the F1 car is -200 m, its initial relative velocity is -10 m/s because the safety car is moving away at 10 m/s, and its relative acceleration is +2 m/s^2. The relative displacement needed to reach zero separation is 200 m, so solve 0=-200-10t+t^2 to find the catch-up time. The separation is largest when the relative velocity changes from negative to zero: v_rel=-10+2t=0, giving t=5 s; add the extra area by which the safety car pulls away, a triangle of base 5 s and height 10 m/s, to the initial 200 m gap to obtain the maximum gap. For the braking phase, start from the catch-up speed of the F1 car, 40 m/s, while the safety car remains at 10 m/s. Draw/use velocity-time areas: during 20 s of braking, the F1’s area is a triangle/trapezoid distance of 400 m, and the safety car’s area is 200 m, so the F1 ends 200 m ahead and stopped. Then the safety car closes the remaining 200 m at 10 m/s in 20 s, giving 40 s total after braking begins.
method.CoT_raw: Use the safety car frame for the first part. Initially the F1 car is 200 m behind, so its relative position is -200 m. Its initial relative velocity is 0 - 10 = -10 m/s, and its relative acceleration is +2 m/s^2. Thus x_rel = -200 - 10t + (1/2)(2)t^2 = -200 - 10t + t^2. Catch-up occurs when x_rel = 0: 0 = -200 - 10t + t^2, so t^2 - 10t - 200 = 0. This gives t = 20 s, rejecting the negative root. The separation is largest when the relative velocity becomes zero: v_rel = -10 + 2t = 0, so t = 5 s. During these 5 s the safety car gains an additional triangular velocity-time area of (1/2)(5)(10) = 25 m, so the maximum separation is 200 + 25 = 225 m. At catch-up, the F1 car speed is v = at = 2(20) = 40 m/s, while the safety car remains at 10 m/s. After braking begins, the F1 car decelerates at 2 m/s^2, so it takes 40/2 = 20 s to stop. In those 20 s, the F1 travels an average-speed distance ((40 + 0)/2)(20) = 400 m, while the safety car travels 10(20) = 200 m. Therefore the F1 is 200 m ahead when it stops. The safety car then closes this 200 m gap at 10 m/s, taking another 20 s. Total time after braking begins is 20 + 20 = 40 s.
